## What the data says
- No thin-fabric test runs exist at 26.5 % O₂, 70.3 kPa (zone **no_evidence**) [PSI-25][PSI-98][PSI-99].
- The predictor gives a physics estimate: adiabatic flame temperature ≈ 2460 K, ~140 K above the hottest thin-fabric microgravity run (≈ 2320 K) and ~450 K above the coldest burning thin-fabric run (≈ 2010 K) [PSI-25].
- Droplet tests are the nearest evidence: 8 methanol droplet runs at 30 % O₂ and 71.2-102.5 kPa sustained burning; evidence coverage 0.545 [PSI-69].
- Fire-resistant materials (Nomex, silicone) did not sustain burning in 5 of 8 runs (3 Nomex burned, 1 did not; 0 silicone burned, 4 did not) at ≤ 22.2 % O₂ and ≈ 101 kPa [PSI-25][PSI-99].
- Outside PSI, Nomex HT90-40 failed NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 at 30 % O₂, 70.1 kPa in 1 g(NTRS 20070018178).
- Partial-gravity data are absent; NASA FM2 researchers note that flame-spread oxygen requirements may be lowest near lunar gravity, so partial gravity could be more hazardous than both micro- and Earth-gravity conditions(NTRS 20260000646).

## How confident we can be
- Evidence coverage for thin fabric is **none** at the target pressure and oxygen; confidence relies solely on the physics estimate.
- Solid-material data are dominated by "sustained" outcomes: 131 of 134 ordinary solid runs were sustained, leaving only 3 non-burning runs, so a flammability limit cannot be located [PSI-25][PSI-98][PSI-99].
- Droplet evidence provides moderate coverage (0.545) for methanol at similar oxygen and pressure, but droplets are not thin fabric.

## Gaps
- No microgravity thin-fabric tests at 26.5 % O₂ or 70 kPa (target pressure outside the 101 kPa range of existing runs).
- No solid-fabric flammability limit data; the dataset lacks sufficient extinction points.
- No partial-gravity (lunar or Martian) combustion data for fabrics.
- Fire-resistant material tests do not include oxygen levels above 22.2 % or the target pressure.

## What future experiments (e.g. LUCI, FM2) should measure
- Thin-fabric ignition and flame-spread runs at 26.5 % O₂ and ~70 kPa in microgravity to replace the physics estimate with direct data.
- Systematic variation of flow speed for thin fabric to map quenching boundaries at the target oxygen level.
- Partial-gravity (0.16 g and 0.38 g) thin-fabric tests to assess whether lower gravity reduces or increases flame-spread hazards.
- Fire-resistant material tests (Nomex, silicone) at ≥ 30 % O₂ and 70 kPa to verify behavior beyond the current ≤ 22 % O₂ limit.
- Additional droplet tests with surrogate fuels on thin fabric substrates to bridge the gap between droplet and solid-fabric behavior.
